transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I... well, I hope I'm not wasting your time, but I've just been having a bit of a hard time lately. 

I wasn't sure if I should even bring it up, but I guess what finally scared me enough to come in is... I've been having these thoughts. I know it sounds awful, and I'm really sorry to even say it out loud, but I just keep thinking it would be so much easier if I just didn't wake up. And... well, sometimes when I'm driving home from the clinic—I'm a vet tech—I catch myself wondering what would happen if I just didn't turn the wheel. 

I know that's a terrible thing to admit, and I promise I don't want to be a bother to anyone. Am I in the right place for this? I just want to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing.
Do you feel like you might act on these thoughts?

Oh, no, no. I really don't think I would. I mean, I would never want to put my husband or the people at the clinic through that. They rely on me. It's more just... a passing thought, you know? Like, I wouldn't actually do it. I just... I get so tired, and the idea of just slipping away and not having to try so hard anymore, it just pops into my head. 

But I haven't made any plans or anything like that. I know it's a bad thing to think, and I'm really trying not to. I just wanted to be honest with you because I want to do this right. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable for several days in a row?

Well... um... I'm not sure if this is exactly what you mean, but... maybe? Earlier this month, I did have a few days where I felt just... almost electrically upbeat. Like I had all this energy, which I know sounds like a good thing, right? 

But then... oh gosh, I feel terrible even admitting this. I ended up snapping at everyone at work over just the tiniest little things. Like, someone misplaced a medication cup, or there was a small change in the morning schedule, and I just... I got so irritable. It wasn't like me at all. I'm usually the one who keeps the peace at the clinic. 

I don't know if that's what you're asking about. I hope that's an okay answer. It was just a few days, and I've been trying so hard to be better since then. Is that the kind of thing you meant?
During those few days when you felt electrically upbeat, did you need much less sleep than usual?

Well, yes... I guess I was sleeping a lot less. But I didn't want anyone to think I was slacking or not taking care of myself! It's just that during that stretch, I was only sleeping maybe... three hours a night? 

I know that sounds bad, and I promise I usually get my full eight hours. But I'd just wake up way before sunrise, and I didn't even feel tired. I actually felt really sharp, like I was totally fine and just didn't need the rest right then. I got so much done around the house before work, so I thought it was okay. 

I hope it's alright that I didn't force myself to stay in bed. I mean, if you feel rested, you should get up, right? Is that... is that a bad thing?
During those days, were you more active than usual or taking on a lot more projects than you normally would?

Well... I suppose I was doing a bit more than usual. I mean, I really wanted to be helpful, you know? I didn't want anyone to think I wasn't pulling my weight. 

So... I did pick up some extra shifts at the clinic. And then, at home, I just sort of... well, I redid our entire household care schedule. I even started calling contractors about some things we've been putting off, and... I guess I was trying to coordinate everyone's tasks like I was running a major hospital project or something. 

I know it sounds like a lot, but I honestly thought I was just being proactive. No one asked me to do all that, and looking back, I hope I wasn't being too pushy or overbearing. I just had all this energy and wanted to make things better for everyone. Is it okay that I tried to do all that? I really was just trying to help.
During those high-energy days, did you feel unusually confident or capable—more than you normally do?

Oh, goodness, no... at least, I really hope I didn't come across that way! I mean, I know I was doing a lot of things, but I didn't feel... you know, smarter or better than anyone else. I would absolutely hate it if anyone at the clinic thought I was being arrogant or full of myself. 

I was really just trying to be useful with all that extra energy. I didn't feel like I was suddenly some superhero or anything like that. I just felt... driven to get my tasks done. I hope I'm answering this right. I just don't think I felt unusually confident, just very, very busy. Is it okay that I didn't have that particular feeling?
During those high-energy days, were you talking more than usual?

Um... no, I don't really think so. I mean, I try really hard to be a good listener, especially at the clinic when I'm dealing with the animals' owners. I would be so embarrassed if I was just... you know, chattering away and not letting anyone else get a word in. 

I don't think my talking was any different. I was definitely moving around a lot and getting things done, but I kept my conversations pretty normal, I think. I really wouldn't want to be a bother to anyone by talking their ear off. 

I hope it's not a problem that I didn't have that happen? I just... I really try to be mindful of other people, even when I'm feeling that energetic. Is that an okay answer?
During those high-energy days, did you find yourself starting a lot more tasks or projects than you usually do?

Well... I suppose I did start a few more things than usual, but I really just wanted to make sure our home was in order. I hope that's alright? 

I mean, after work, I just... I had a hard time sitting down and relaxing. I would find myself sort of walking through the house, just trying to see what needed fixing or improving. I started measuring the rooms and making all these lists of things to do... and then I ended up reorganizing the kitchen cabinets. 

I know it sounds a little silly, doing all that late at night when everyone else was asleep, but I just wanted everything to be nice for my family. I really wasn't trying to be disruptive or anything. I just couldn't quite sit still, and I thought I might as well be productive. Is it normal to want to tidy up like that when you have extra energy? I hope I didn't overdo it.
During those high-energy days, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive for you?

Oh... um. Well, I really try to be responsible, you know? Especially with our finances. I would never want to put my family in a bad spot on purpose. 

But... I guess I did do something a little bit out of character. I just... I got so worried about the older animals we see at the clinic, and I started thinking about how we could make things better for them at home, too. So I... well, I bought some things. Just some monitoring equipment, and some special ramps and orthopaedic bedding. 

At the time, it just felt so incredibly urgent, like I absolutely had to get these supplies right that second to help them. It felt like the right thing to do, I promise. But... um, looking back, I kind of put a lot of charges on our credit card. And... we really can't cover them right now. 

I feel just awful about it. I'm usually so careful with money. I hope you don't think I'm completely reckless? I really was just trying to help, but I know I made a mistake. Is it... is it common to make silly decisions like that when you're feeling that way?
About that high-energy, upbeat and irritable stretch earlier this month—did it last at least four days in a row?

Oh, um... four days? I'm not really sure, honestly. I wasn't exactly keeping track of the days... I hope that's okay? 

I just remember it was a stretch where I was getting a lot done around the house, like I mentioned. But I don't know if it was exactly four days in a row. It might have been a few days, or maybe it just felt like a long weekend? I really try to stay balanced most of the time, so maybe it wasn't quite that long. 

Is it important that it was exactly four days? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, but I just... I really can't say for certain. I'm sorry if I'm not being very helpful with that.
During that high-energy stretch, did it cause problems at work or at home that other people noticed?

Oh... um... problems? I really try my best not to be a burden on anyone, I promise. I want to be a good employee and a good wife. 

But... I guess... well, my husband did notice. He's been so wonderful, really. He's had to sort of... take over a lot of things at home. Like paying the bills and making sure we have meals, because I just... I haven't been quite myself. And he checks on me a lot, just to make sure I'm safe, especially when my thoughts get a little... dark. I feel so guilty making him worry like that.

And at the clinic... well, I've always prided myself on being very careful, but I've started making a few little mistakes here and there. Nothing terrible, I hope! But enough that I've been kind of avoiding my friends and coworkers. I just... I get so worried that I might snap at them if I'm feeling irritable, or that I might just completely fall apart in front of them. 

I really didn't mean to let things slide so much. Is it normal to feel this overwhelmed and let things slip when you're going through this? I just want to get back to being reliable again.
During that high-energy stretch, did other people say you were talking unusually fast or that they had trouble interrupting you?

Oh, um... talking fast? I don't think so. I really try to be a good listener, you know? Especially at the clinic, it's so important to hear what the pet owners are saying. 

I mean, maybe I was a little more... enthusiastic than usual about some of the ideas I had? But nobody ever told me I was talking too fast or that they couldn't get a word in. I would feel just terrible if I was talking over people or making them feel like they couldn't speak. I always want to be polite. 

I don't think I was doing that, but... maybe I just didn't notice? I hope I wasn't being rude. Does that sound like I'm answering your question okay? I really don't think that was happening with me.
For the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Oh... well, I really try to keep a brave face, you know? I don't want to bring anyone down. But... yes, I suppose I have been feeling quite low lately. 

It's just... most days, it feels like all the color has just drained out of everything. Even when the house is bustling and there's a lot going on around me, I just feel this... heaviness. I actually find myself hiding in the laundry room sometimes, just to cry. I just can't stand the thought of anyone seeing me like that, looking so... hopeless. I feel awful even admitting it. 

I know I should be stronger, and I really am trying my best to stay positive. Is it okay that I'm feeling this way? I hope I'm not making things sound worse than they are, I just want to give you the right picture of what's been happening.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Oh... well... I feel a bit awful admitting this, because I know I have a good life and I should just be grateful. I really do try to keep busy and stay engaged. But... yes, I suppose I have. 

I usually have so many little things that bring me joy outside of the clinic. But lately... I just haven't even touched my camera. And I haven't checked the bird feeders with any real interest, or... or even cared what’s coming up in the garden right now. 

It's actually... um, it's a little frightening for me to say out loud. Because those things, they used to be how I felt like myself, you know? And now it's just... blank. I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or unappreciative of my life. I really am trying to find the joy in things again. Does that... does that make sense to you? Am I explaining that okay?
Have you ever had a time when your mood was so high or irritable that you had to be hospitalized?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I've never had to go to the hospital for anything like that. 

I mean, I know I mentioned feeling a little more energetic or enthusiastic sometimes, but it never got out of hand or anything where I needed that kind of help. I really try to keep things manageable and not let my moods become a burden to anyone else. 

I would be so mortified if things ever got to a point where I had to be hospitalized. I always try to stay on top of things, you know? I hope it didn't sound like I was totally out of control before. I'm doing my best to be a good patient and keep everything steady. Does that answer your question all right?
During that high-energy irritable period, did it make you miss work or keep you from doing your usual responsibilities?

Oh... well... I want to say no, because I really do pride myself on being reliable. I hate the idea of letting people down. But... if I'm being completely honest... it has been affecting things. 

I... I've actually started making some mistakes at the clinic. Just little things, but... enough that it worries me. And I've been avoiding my friends lately. I'm just so afraid I'm either going to snap at them over nothing, or just completely fall apart crying. I wouldn't want to put them through that. 

And at home... oh, it's so embarrassing to admit... my husband has had to take over almost everything. The bills, the cooking... and just keeping an eye on me, making sure I'm safe when... when my thoughts get really dark. I feel terrible putting all that on him. I should be able to handle my own life, shouldn't I? I hope you don't think I'm just giving up... I really am trying to hold it together. Is it normal for it to get this bad?
During that energetic and irritable stretch, did other people clearly notice that you were acting differently from your usual self?

Oh... um, no, I don't think so. I really try my hardest not to let my moods spill over and affect anyone else. 

I mean, my husband might have noticed I was getting a little more... enthusiastically organized around the house, maybe? But I always try to keep a smile on my face and just be my normal self at the clinic. I would hate for anyone at work to think I was being unprofessional or difficult to be around. 

I really do make an effort to keep it all under wraps so I don't bother anyone. I hope that's the right way to handle it... I mean, I try to be very considerate of how I'm coming across to others. Does that make sense? I haven't been acting out in public or anything like that, I promise.
Thinking about that energetic and irritable spell earlier this month, did it last four full days in a row?

Oh... four full days? Um... I don't really think it was that long. I mean, I would feel just awful if I let myself be that way for nearly a whole week. 

I always try to pull myself together much faster than that, you know? Just so I'm not being a nuisance to my husband or anyone else. It felt more like... maybe just a day or two of feeling a bit too wound up before I managed to settle back down. I really do try my best to nip those moods in the bud so I can get back to being helpful and reliable. 

I hope it's all right that I didn't keep an exact count of the days... I'm really trying to give you the most accurate answers I can. Is it okay if I'm not entirely sure about the exact timeframe?
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?

Oh... um... yes. I mean, I really wish I could say no, because I know how exhausting it must be for everyone around me when I get like this. But... if I'm being completely honest with you... this feeling hasn't just been for a couple of weeks. 

It's actually been... well, it's been hanging over me for about 11 months now. Even before this past month when things just got so unbearable and my husband had to step in so much. I've been trying so hard to just push through it and go to the clinic and be a good wife, but... it's just been there, like a heavy cloud, for almost a year. 

I'm so sorry, I probably should have mentioned that sooner. I just feel so ashamed that I haven't been able to snap out of it for that long. I really have been trying my best to get better on my own so I wouldn't have to bother anyone with it. I hope you don't think I'm just wallowing in it... I really do want to get back to my old self. Is it... is it helpful that I'm telling you this now?
